niche.habitat: Volcanic scree slopes, fog belts, shallow shelf edges
niche.diet: Opportunistic omnivore; crushes calcified fungi, catches falling fruit, scavenges carrion

body: Bivalve-convergent lineage. Fused, flattened carapace of chitin-mineral composite. Four lateral walking legs with stiff joints. Massive asymmetrical claws. Visceral mass retracts fully under shield. Copper-veined hemolymph visible through translucent carapace edge.

links: Flattened profile minimizes drag in dense air and lowers center of mass under high gravity
High density increases drag force; high gravity increases toppling torque

skill.effect: Locks claws into substrate, reducing incoming damage by 30% and preventing displacement.

chains.weakness: Slow to right itself if overturned.
observe: Carapaz flattens against rock during gusts.
Scree shifts under its weight without it tipping.

journal.en: The pressure and gravity demanded a low profile; everything else followed.

plausibility.summary: On 1.85 g (F4), a low, wide body lowers the center of mass and cuts overturning torque on scree; in ~10 bar, dense air (F8) raises form drag on tall profiles, favouring a flattened shield. Chitin–mineral composites are a standard way to buy stiffness per unit mass at high structural loads—same scaling logic as exoskeletal armouring on Earth.
fixes: On 1.85 g (F4), a low, wide body lowers the center of mass and cuts overturning torque on scree; in ~10 bar, dense air (F8) raises form drag on tall profiles, favouring a flattened shield. Chitin–mineral composites are a standard way to buy stiffness per unit mass at high structural loads—same scaling logic as exoskeletal armouring on Earth.

analogues.organism: Brachyuran carcinisation (flat, wide carapace); limpets and chitons (profile hugging rock); trilobite/concave dorsal shields for streamlining against flow or wind.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Lateral leg joints and sideways gait
links: Sideways gait maximizes stability on steep volcanic scree and allows air-rudder thrust
Lateral movement avoids leg crossing on shifting scree; dense air provides lateral lift/drag
F18: Steep volcanic slopes, loose scree

skill.effect: Move 3 meters sideways instantly, ignoring terrain penalties. Dodges frontal attacks.

chains.weakness: Cannot retreat quickly in forward direction.
observe: Legs never cross the midline while moving.
Creature pushes off air to steer.

journal.en: Sideways is the only way; the ground shifts and the wind pushes.

plausibility.summary: Keep sideways gait; root it in leg joint geometry, wide stance, and claw purchase on loose scree. Reframe F8 as slight gust buffering or reduced wind heeling on a flat carapace, not “air-rudder thrust.” Scuttle Dash can stay a game ability if described as explosive sideways leg drive, not aerodynamic push.
fixes: Keep sideways gait; root it in leg joint geometry, wide stance, and claw purchase on loose scree. Reframe F8 as slight gust buffering or reduced wind heeling on a flat carapace, not “air-rudder thrust.” Scuttle Dash can stay a game ability if described as explosive sideways leg drive, not aerodynamic push.

analogues.organism: Brachyuran crabs—lateral leg orientation and alternating tetrapod sideways gait on irregular substrate (mechanical stability, not wing-like lift).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Heavy claws function as ballast, anchors, and instant traps for gravity-accelerated prey
High drag air demands grip; high gravity increases prey fall velocity

skill.effect: Pins target, dealing 12 damage and reducing target movement by 40% for 2 turns.

chains.weakness: Claws are heavy; slow recovery time.
observe: Claws catch a falling fruit mid-air.
Claws act as ballast on steep slope.
One claw is larger than the other.

journal.en: Gravity does the work; the claws just catch.

plausibility.summary: Under 1.85 g, perched prey and detritus accelerate faster when dislodged, making ambush at a scree edge or shelf lip selectively favourable. Heavy chelae add anchoring mass and grip on steep volcanic slopes (F18); asymmetry matches a major/minor tool division (crush anchor vs trap) without demanding two equally costly weapons. Cost is metabolic and manoeuvre: heavy distal mass slows strike recovery—consistent with the stated weakness.
fixes: Under 1.85 g, perched prey and detritus accelerate faster when dislodged, making ambush at a scree edge or shelf lip selectively favourable. Cost is metabolic and manoeuvre: heavy distal mass slows strike recovery—consistent with the stated weakness.

analogues.organism: Stone and coconut crabs (crushing chelae, asymmetry); robber crab holding posture on slopes; general major/minor chela division in decapods.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Visceral mass retracts completely under shield
links: Tucked abdomen shields delicate gills from abrasive volcanic ash and conserves heat in fog
Volcanic activity suspends abrasive particulates; fog reduces temperature and increases humidity

skill.effect: Hides from detection. Regenerates health slowly. Vulnerable to high-pitch sound.

chains.weakness: Cannot breathe fully when curled; slow to emerge.

journal.en: When the fog comes, the Carapaz becomes a stone.

plausibility.summary: Optional honesty tweak: cite closure against ash and abrasion first; mention fog as secondary thermal/humidity trigger. Do not lean on piezolytes for fog curling unless the species routinely experiences large hydrostatic swings.

body_plan.origin: Modified pedal lobes from bivalve-like ancestor

temperament: Cautious, territorial, anchors deeply; slow to engage but relentless once committed
secrets: Their copper-rich blood neutralizes sulfide toxins from volcanic vents.
They can detect pressure changes in the air to predict fog fronts hours in advance.
moments: When the amber fog rolls in, the scree goes silent as a dozen Carapaz lock their claws into the stone and vanish into their shells, leaving only the rhythmic hiss of ventilation and the faint blue glow of their copper blood.

journal.en: They walk sideways because the wind and the scree leave no other way.
A wink at carcinisation? No; just the physics of 1.85g and 10 bar squeezing everything flat and lateral.
